questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Congenital talipes equinovarus is the formal name; 'talipes' derives from talus + pes.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The hindfoot is in equinus and varus; the full deformity is remembered as CAVE.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The navicular subluxates medially on the head of the talus, producing midfoot adduction.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The forefoot is adducted, not abducted; abduction is part of the Ponseti correction.

questions.pearl: CTEV deformity order (CAVE): Cavus, Adductus, Varus, Equinus; Ponseti casting corrects them in that order.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Assessment of growth in a child:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Mid-upper arm circumference is an age-independent anthropometric screen; <11.5 cm (6-59 months) indicates severe acute malnutrition.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Occipitofrontal circumference reflects brain growth and is plotted routinely up to 2-3 years.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Recumbent length (under 2 years) or height is a core growth parameter; low length-for-age means stunting.

options.label: D
options.explanation: IQ assesses cognitive development, not physical growth.

questions.pearl: Growth = physical size (weight, length, OFC, MUAC); development = acquisition of skills (milestones, IQ).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Causes of maternal mortality in Bangladesh:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Eclampsia is the second leading direct cause of maternal death in Bangladesh after haemorrhage (BMMS).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Puerperal sepsis contributes, but in Bangladeshi maternal mortality surveys it ranks well below haemorrhage, eclampsia and obstructed labour.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Twins raise obstetric risk but are not themselves a recorded cause of maternal death.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Uterine rupture from obstructed labour causes haemorrhage and death, especially with home deliveries.

questions.pearl: Leading cause of maternal death in Bangladesh: haemorrhage (mainly PPH), followed by eclampsia.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Causes of under-5 mortality in Bangladesh:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pneumonia/ARI is the leading infectious killer of under-5 children in Bangladesh.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Birth asphyxia is a major cause of neonatal death, which forms most under-5 deaths.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Thalassaemia is a chronic disease burden but not a leading cause of under-5 mortality.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Malnutrition underlies a large share of child deaths by worsening pneumonia and diarrhoea.

questions.pearl: Most under-5 deaths in Bangladesh are neonatal: prematurity, birth asphyxia and neonatal sepsis lead the list.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Causes of white patch in the throat:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Diphtheria forms a greyish-white adherent pseudomembrane that bleeds on removal.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Fusospirochaetal infection forms a greyish membrane over a tonsillar ulcer.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Viral pharyngitis usually causes diffuse congestion without a membrane.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Candida forms creamy white plaques that wipe off, leaving a raw red base.

questions.pearl: Membrane over tonsil: diphtheria, Vincent's angina, infectious mononucleosis, follicular tonsillitis, candidiasis, agranulocytosis.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hyperoestrogenism and reduced testosterone in cirrhosis cause testicular atrophy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: In women, hormonal disturbance in CLD may cause breast atrophy and menstrual irregularity.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Raised oestrogen causes vasodilatation of the thenar and hypothenar eminences.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Increased oestrogen/androgen ratio (and spironolactone) causes gynaecomastia in men.

questions.pearl: Stigmata of CLD: spider naevi (>5), palmar erythema, gynaecomastia, testicular atrophy, Dupuytren's, caput medusae.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: CMV can cause hepatitis but is not a primary hepatotropic virus; it infects many organs.

options.label: B
options.explanation: EBV causes hepatitis in infectious mononucleosis but primarily targets B cells.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hepatitis A is a primary hepatotropic picornavirus, spread faeco-orally.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hepatitis C is a primary hepatotropic flavivirus causing chronic hepatitis in most infected people.

questions.pearl: Primary hepatotropic viruses: A, B, C, D, E; HBV is the only DNA virus among them.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Candida is a commensal that causes thrush and invasive disease in immunosuppression.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Classic opportunist causing meningitis in AIDS with CD4 <100.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Histoplasma is a dimorphic endemic (primary) pathogen, though it disseminates in AIDS.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Varicella zoster is a virus, not a fungus.

questions.pearl: Opportunistic fungi: Candida, Cryptococcus, Aspergillus, Mucor, Pneumocystis jirovecii.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: B cells internalise antigen via surface Ig and present it on MHC II.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Dendritic cells are the most potent professional APCs, priming naive T cells.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Neutrophils are phagocytes but do not act as professional APCs; they lack constitutive MHC II.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Basophils release histamine in type I hypersensitivity; they are not APCs.

questions.pearl: Professional APCs (express MHC II): dendritic cells, macrophages and B cells.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pyogenic osteomyelitis is a bacterial bone infection, usually haematogenous in children.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Staphylococcus aureus causes most cases at all ages.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Dead bone (sequestrum) separates and is surrounded by new periosteal bone (involucrum).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Acute haematogenous osteomyelitis is typically a disease of children, in metaphyses of long bones.

questions.pearl: Salmonella osteomyelitis is classic in sickle cell disease; Staph aureus remains commonest overall.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: The aphakic pupil is jet black and normal-sized; iridodonesis and a deep anterior chamber are typical.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Without the lens, accommodation is lost completely.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Loss of the lens filter lets more blue light through, causing cyanopsia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The eye becomes highly hypermetropic (about +10 D), blurring both distance and near vision.

questions.pearl: Aphakia signs: deep anterior chamber, iridodonesis, jet-black pupil, only two Purkinje images.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: AOM causes primary otalgia arising in the ear itself.

options.label: B
options.text: Carcinoma of the base of tongue
options.explanation: Pain is referred to the ear via the glossopharyngeal nerve (Jacobson's branch).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pain is referred via the vagus (Arnold's nerve).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Inflammation of the tympanic membrane is a local cause of earache.

questions.pearl: Referred otalgia nerves: V, VII, IX, X and C2-C3; normal ear with earache in a smoker means look for cancer.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Immature forms are few (usually <10%, often <5%), unlike leukaemia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Platelet production is preserved; thrombocytopenia suggests leukaemia instead.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Leukaemoid reaction implies a count above about 50,000/mm3; 10,000 is merely the upper normal limit.

options.label: D
options.text: Bone marrow shows mild myeloid hyperplasia
options.explanation: The marrow is reactively hypercellular but without blast excess.

questions.pearl: Leukaemoid vs CML: high LAP score, no Philadelphia chromosome and toxic granulation favour leukaemoid reaction.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Clotting factors are normal, so clotting time is normal.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Bleeding time is prolonged because of thrombocytopenia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Extrinsic pathway is intact; PT is normal.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Intrinsic pathway is intact; APTT is normal.

questions.pearl: ITP: isolated low platelets, prolonged BT, normal PT/APTT, increased megakaryocytes in marrow.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Radial nerve injury (e.g. spiral groove) paralyses wrist and finger extensors.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Saturday night palsy is compression of the radial nerve in the spiral groove.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Ulnar nerve palsy paralyses medial lumbricals and interossei, clawing the ring and little fingers.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Winging is due to long thoracic nerve injury paralysing serratus anterior.

questions.pearl: Ape-thumb deformity is median nerve; foot drop is common peroneal nerve.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: SARS-CoV-2 is an enveloped positive-sense single-stranded RNA coronavirus.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Bilateral peripheral ground-glass opacities are the typical CT finding.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Fever is the commonest symptom and may be high grade.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Overall case fatality is low (around 1-3%), though higher in the elderly and those with comorbidity.

questions.pearl: SARS-CoV-2 enters cells via ACE2 receptors; RT-PCR of a nasopharyngeal swab is the diagnostic standard.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Bacterial infection produces mucopurulent discharge with sticky lids in the morning.

options.label: B
options.text: Most common cause is Staphylococcus aureus
options.explanation: Staph aureus is the commonest organism in acute mucopurulent conjunctivitis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: It typically starts in one eye but quickly becomes bilateral.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Key corrected: uncomplicated acute bacterial conjunctivitis usually resolves in 10-14 days even without treatment (Khurana, Kanski); antibiotics shorten it.

questions.pearl: Hyperacute purulent conjunctivitis suggests gonococcus, which can perforate the cornea; it is not self-limiting.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: C-reactive protein rises rapidly with IL-6 driven hepatic synthesis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: SAA is a major positive acute phase reactant; chronic elevation causes AA amyloidosis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Neutrophils are cells, not plasma proteins, although they rise in inflammation.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Ferritin is a positive acute phase protein, so it may be normal despite iron deficiency in inflammation.

questions.pearl: Negative acute phase proteins fall in inflammation: albumin, transferrin, transthyretin.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Gastric pepsin is an aspartic endopeptidase that begins protein digestion.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Alpha-1 antitrypsin is a protease inhibitor that protects lungs from neutrophil elastase.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Renin is an aspartyl protease that cleaves angiotensinogen to angiotensin I.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Trypsin is a pancreatic serine protease that also activates other zymogens.

questions.pearl: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency causes panacinar emphysema and liver cirrhosis (PiZZ phenotype).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: O2 is not consumed in the urea cycle; urea's oxygen atom comes from CO2.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Free ammonia combines with CO2 to form carbamoyl phosphate, providing one nitrogen.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Bicarbonate/CO2 supplies the carbon of urea via carbamoyl phosphate.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Urea carries two nitrogens: one from ammonia, one from aspartate.

questions.pearl: Rate-limiting enzyme of the urea cycle: carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I, activated by N-acetylglutamate.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Crotamiton 10% is a scabicide with antipruritic action.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Fluconazole is an antifungal with no activity against mites.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Oral ivermectin (200 microgram/kg, repeated) treats scabies, especially crusted scabies.

options.label: D
options.explanation: DEC is used for filariasis, not scabies.

questions.pearl: First-line topical scabicide: permethrin 5% applied neck down, repeated after 7 days; treat all contacts.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Ascending infection in men causes acute epididymo-orchitis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Gonococcus is a classic cause of bartholinitis and abscess.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Ascending infection causes PID with risk of tubal infertility and ectopic pregnancy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Gonococcal urethritis may extend to cause acute prostatitis.

questions.pearl: Disseminated gonococcal infection: tenosynovitis, migratory polyarthralgia and pustular skin lesions.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: CA 15-3 (and CA 27-29) is the breast marker; CA 19-9 is for pancreatic cancer.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Prostate-specific antigen is the standard prostate cancer marker.

options.label: C
options.explanation: CEA is raised in adenocarcinomas of colon, lung, pancreas, stomach and breast.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Calcitonin marks medullary carcinoma (C cells); thyroglobulin marks follicular cancer.

questions.pearl: Thyroglobulin is used to monitor recurrence after total thyroidectomy for differentiated (papillary/follicular) thyroid cancer.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Tetracyclines stain fetal teeth, impair bone growth and cause maternal hepatotoxicity.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Doxycycline is a tetracycline and shares the same fetal risks.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Penicillins are among the safest antibiotics in pregnancy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cephalosporins are considered safe throughout pregnancy.

questions.pearl: Avoid in pregnancy: tetracyclines, aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, chloramphenicol (grey baby), co-trimoxazole near term.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: SARS-CoV-2 spreads by respiratory droplets and aerosols, not mosquitoes.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Zika virus is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes and causes congenital microcephaly.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Chikungunya is transmitted by Aedes aegypti and albopictus; it causes severe arthralgia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Yellow fever is an Aedes-borne flavivirus; it has an effective live vaccine.

questions.pearl: Aedes transmits dengue, chikungunya, Zika and yellow fever; Culex transmits filaria and Japanese encephalitis.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Naproxen is a propionic acid derivative NSAID with a long half-life.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Ibuprofen is a propionic acid NSAID with the lowest GI risk among non-selective NSAIDs.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Ceftibuten is an oral third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Ketorolac is a potent analgesic NSAID used parenterally for severe pain, limited to 5 days.

questions.pearl: NSAIDs inhibit COX; COX-2 selective agents (celecoxib, etoricoxib) reduce GI toxicity but increase CV risk.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Azole antifungals are CYP3A4 inhibitors.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Rifampicin is a potent CYP450 inducer, reducing OCP, warfarin and antiretroviral levels.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Barbiturates induce hepatic microsomal enzymes and their own metabolism.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Metronidazole inhibits warfarin metabolism and causes a disulfiram-like reaction.

questions.pearl: Enzyme inducers mnemonic GPRS Cell Phone: Griseofulvin, Phenytoin, Rifampicin, Smoking, Carbamazepine, Phenobarbitone.

questions.subject: Gynecology
questions.stem: Screening tests for carcinoma of the cervix:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Visual inspection with acetic acid is the national screening method in Bangladesh (aceto-white areas).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Cervical cytology is the classic screening test for CIN.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Biopsy is the confirmatory diagnostic test, not a screening test.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Colposcopy is used as a secondary screening step in screen-positive women to direct biopsy.

questions.pearl: Bangladesh cervical screening: VIA for women 30-60 years; HPV 16 and 18 cause about 70% of cervical cancers.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Bleeding into the cyst causes sudden pain and enlargement.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Rupture of a mucinous cystadenoma may seed mucin-secreting cells through the peritoneum.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Rupture may follow trauma or torsion, causing peritonitis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Secondary infection may follow torsion or occur postpartum.

questions.pearl: Commonest complication of benign ovarian tumour: torsion, especially with dermoid cysts.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Major (type IV) placenta praevia makes vaginal delivery impossible and dangerous.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Two previous sections is a relative indication; repeat CS is usual but not obligatory.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Fetal distress is a relative indication; delivery route depends on the stage of labour.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Abruption is often delivered vaginally after ARM, especially with fetal death.

questions.pearl: Absolute CS indications: central placenta praevia, contracted pelvis (CPD), obstructing pelvic mass, advanced cervical cancer.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: M. kansasii is a non-tuberculous (atypical) photochromogen.

options.label: B
options.explanation: M. avium complex is a non-tuberculous mycobacterium causing disease in AIDS.

options.label: C
options.explanation: M. bovis belongs to the complex; BCG is an attenuated strain of it.

options.label: D
options.explanation: M. tuberculosis is the prototype member of the complex.

questions.pearl: MTB complex: M. tuberculosis, M. bovis, M. africanum, M. microti, M. canetti.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Transudative pleural effusion is caused by:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Raised hydrostatic pressure in CCF is the commonest cause of transudate.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Parapneumonic effusion is an exudate.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Malignant effusions are exudates.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Myxoedema can cause a transudative effusion.

questions.pearl: Light's criteria: exudate if pleural/serum protein >0.5, LDH ratio >0.6, or pleural LDH >2/3 upper normal.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: ARF typically causes hyperkalaemia due to reduced excretion.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Corticosteroids have mineralocorticoid action, increasing renal K+ loss.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Stool is rich in potassium; chronic diarrhoea depletes body K+.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Salt loss in sweat causes hypochloraemic metabolic alkalosis with hypokalaemia.

questions.pearl: Hypokalaemia ECG: flat T waves, U waves, ST depression; correct K+ before giving insulin in DKA.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: BCC invades and destroys local tissues but rarely metastasises.

options.label: B
options.explanation: BCC is slow growing over months to years.

options.label: C
options.explanation: UV exposure is the main risk factor; it occurs on sun-exposed skin.

options.label: D
options.explanation: About 90% occur on the face, above a line from angle of mouth to ear lobe.

questions.pearl: BCC: pearly rolled edge with telangiectasia; treat by excision with 3-4 mm margin or Mohs surgery.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Enteric fever causes ileal perforation and haemorrhage, not obstruction.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Salmonella can cause septic arthritis and osteomyelitis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Acute cholecystitis may occur; the gallbladder is the site of chronic carriage.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Toxic myocarditis is a recognised complication.

questions.pearl: Commonest serious enteric complication: ileal perforation in the third week, at Peyer's patches near the terminal ileum.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Low stroke volume with compensatory tachycardia gives a rapid, low-volume pulse.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Shock causes hypotension; blood pressure falls late in children.

options.label: C
options.explanation: CRT >2-3 seconds indicates poor peripheral perfusion.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Tachycardia is the earliest compensatory sign of hypovolaemia.

questions.pearl: IMCI shock in a child: cold hands plus CRT >3 seconds plus weak fast pulse.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Muscarinic blockade causes dry mouth, not salivation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Cholestatic jaundice is an idiosyncratic hepatic reaction (e.g. chlorpromazine), not a muscarinic-blockade effect.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Reduced gut motility from vagal blockade causes constipation.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Detrusor relaxation causes retention, especially with prostatic enlargement.

questions.pearl: Anticholinergic toxicity: hot as a hare, dry as a bone, red as a beet, blind as a bat, mad as a hatter.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Elapid (cobra, krait) venom contains neurotoxins causing descending paralysis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Sea snake venom is myotoxic, causing rhabdomyolysis and myoglobinuria.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Russell's viper venom causes acute kidney injury.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Viper venom contains proteolytic enzymes causing local swelling and necrosis.

questions.pearl: Krait bite is often painless with no local signs but causes severe neuroparalysis; give polyvalent ASV.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Oral ulcers are features of B-complex or vitamin C deficiency, not vitamin A.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Keratinisation of skin around hair follicles produces toad skin.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Keratinising metaplasia of the urinary tract epithelium predisposes to calculi and haematuria.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Xerophthalmia (night blindness, Bitot's spots, keratomalacia) is the classic feature.

questions.pearl: WHO xerophthalmia: XN night blindness, X1B Bitot's spots, X3 keratomalacia; give 200,000 IU on days 1, 2 and 14.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Citalopram is an SSRI; it can prolong the QT interval at high doses.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Sertraline is an SSRI, preferred after MI.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Mirtazapine is an alpha-2 antagonist (NaSSA).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Phenelzine is a non-selective MAO inhibitor.

questions.pearl: SSRI plus MAOI or tramadol risks serotonin syndrome; fluoxetine is the SSRI licensed in adolescents.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: d-tubocurarine is the prototype non-depolarising neuromuscular blocker.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Atracurium is non-depolarising, eliminated by Hofmann degradation, good in renal/hepatic failure.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Lidocaine is a local anaesthetic and class Ib antiarrhythmic, not a muscle relaxant.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Suxamethonium is the depolarising relaxant of choice for rapid sequence intubation.

questions.pearl: Suxamethonium risks: hyperkalaemia, malignant hyperthermia and scoline apnoea in pseudocholinesterase deficiency.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Fissure causes sharp pain on defecation with a streak of bright red blood.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Key corrected: rectal polyps cause painless bleeding as rectal mucosa above the dentate line lacks somatic pain fibres.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Uncomplicated internal piles bleed painlessly, but thrombosed or prolapsed piles and external haemorrhoids are painful.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Colorectal cancer typically causes painless bleeding with change in bowel habit.

questions.pearl: Below the dentate line is somatically innervated and painful; lesions above it bleed painlessly.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Sublingual/submental dermoid cysts lie in the midline.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Thyroglossal cyst is midline and moves with tongue protrusion.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Branchial cyst lies laterally at the anterior border of sternocleidomastoid.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cystic hygroma lies in the posterior triangle and is brilliantly transilluminant.

questions.pearl: Thyroglossal cyst moves upward on tongue protrusion; Sistrunk's operation removes the central hyoid body.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Papillary carcinoma accounts for about 70-80% of thyroid cancers.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Childhood neck irradiation is the strongest risk factor (e.g. Chernobyl).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Differentiated tumour takes up iodine; RAI ablates remnants and metastases after thyroidectomy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Papillary carcinoma spreads via lymphatics, unlike follicular which spreads by blood.

questions.pearl: Papillary carcinoma: psammoma bodies and Orphan Annie nuclei; best prognosis of thyroid cancers.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Insulin inhibits hormone-sensitive lipase.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Insulin suppresses hepatic gluconeogenic enzymes such as PEPCK.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Insulin activates glucokinase, PFK-1 and pyruvate kinase.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Insulin is anabolic and increases protein synthesis and amino acid uptake.

questions.pearl: Insulin drives K+ into cells via Na+/K+-ATPase, the basis of insulin-dextrose for hyperkalaemia.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.text: Folic acid is a maturation factor
options.explanation: Folate and B12 are needed for DNA synthesis in erythroblast maturation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Mature RBCs lack mitochondria and rely on glycolysis for ATP.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Mature RBCs lack a nucleus and cannot divide.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Haemoglobin fills about one-third of the RBC by weight and carries oxygen.

questions.pearl: RBC lifespan is 120 days; reticulocytes still contain ribosomal RNA and mature in 1-2 days in blood.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Raising gastric pH keeps iron in the poorly absorbed ferric form.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Dietary fat does not enhance non-haem iron absorption.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Phosphates and phytates form insoluble complexes that reduce absorption.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Vitamin C reduces ferric to ferrous iron and forms a soluble chelate.

questions.pearl: Iron is absorbed mainly in the duodenum; hepcidin blocks ferroportin to reduce absorption.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: A left-shifted curve means haemoglobin binds O2 more tightly (lower P50).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Raised CO2 (Bohr effect) shifts the curve right, lowering saturation at a given PO2.

options.label: C
options.text: Exercise causes a left shift of the O2 dissociation curve
options.explanation: Exercise raises temperature, CO2, H+ and 2,3-DPG, all shifting the curve right.

options.label: D
options.text: Raised temperature causes a right shift of the curve
options.explanation: Heat reduces Hb-O2 affinity, aiding O2 delivery to active tissues.

questions.pearl: Right shift factors (CADET face right): CO2, Acid, 2,3-DPG, Exercise, Temperature.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Venous congestion causes a plethoric, cyanosed face, not oligaemia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Dyspnoea is the commonest symptom, from airway oedema or tumour compression.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Facial and upper limb oedema occur due to impaired venous return.

options.label: D
options.explanation: SVC obstruction affects the upper body; IVC is a separate entity.

questions.pearl: Commonest cause of SVC obstruction: lung cancer (small cell) followed by lymphoma.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Microaneurysms are the earliest clinically visible sign.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Lipid leakage from damaged capillaries forms yellow hard exudates.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Papilloedema reflects raised intracranial pressure (or malignant hypertension), not diabetes.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Deep intraretinal haemorrhages are typical of background retinopathy.

questions.pearl: Proliferative DR is defined by neovascularisation; treat with panretinal photocoagulation or anti-VEGF.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Conditions to which HIV-infected patients are susceptible:

options.label: A
options.explanation: An AIDS-defining infection when CD4 falls below 100 cells/mm3.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Direct HIV brain involvement causes cognitive and motor decline.

options.label: C
options.explanation: PCP occurs with CD4 <200; co-trimoxazole prophylaxis prevents it.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Invasive cervical cancer is AIDS-defining due to persistent HPV infection.

questions.pearl: Start co-trimoxazole prophylaxis when CD4 <200 cells/mm3 to prevent PCP and toxoplasmosis.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.text: Evaluate and clearly define the patient's problem
options.explanation: Step 1 of the WHO Guide to Good Prescribing.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Step 2: state what you want to achieve with treatment.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Steps 3-4: verify suitability of the P-drug and start treatment.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Step 6: monitor and stop or adjust therapy as needed.

questions.pearl: WHO 6 steps: define problem, specify objective, verify P-drug, start treatment, give information, monitor.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Marrow examination assesses infiltration and prognosis in CLL.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Marrow (preferably trephine) is examined for staging of Hodgkin lymphoma.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Marrow plasma cells >10% is a diagnostic criterion for myeloma.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pneumonia is diagnosed clinically and radiologically; marrow study has no role.

questions.pearl: Other marrow indications: unexplained cytopenias, aplastic anaemia, leukaemia, PUO, kala-azar (LD bodies).

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Severe haemorrhage causes tachypnoea and air hunger from tissue hypoxia and acidosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Blindness is not a feature of acute haemorrhage.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Sympathetic vasoconstriction diverts blood from the skin, making extremities cold.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cutaneous vasoconstriction and loss of red cells produce pallor.

questions.pearl: Class III haemorrhage (30-40% loss) is the first stage in which systolic blood pressure falls.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Muscles supplied by the trigeminal nerve:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Supplied by the mandibular division (V3).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Supplied by V3; it opens the mouth and protrudes the mandible.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Deltoid is supplied by the axillary nerve (C5, C6).

options.label: D
options.explanation: The posterior belly is supplied by the facial nerve; the anterior belly by V3.

questions.pearl: V3 supplies muscles of mastication, mylohyoid, anterior digastric, tensor tympani and tensor veli palatini.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: RNA is usually single stranded, though it may fold into hairpins; dsRNA occurs in some viruses.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Cellular RNA (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA) is single stranded.

options.label: C
options.explanation: RNA contains ribose with a 2'-OH group, unlike deoxyribose in DNA.

options.label: D
options.explanation: mRNA, tRNA and rRNA all take part in translation.

questions.pearl: RNA contains uracil instead of thymine; the 2'-OH makes RNA less stable than DNA.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Small cell lung cancer secretes ACTH causing ectopic Cushing's syndrome.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Calcitonin is produced by medullary thyroid cancer and some lung cancers.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Carcinoid tumours secrete serotonin causing flushing and diarrhoea.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Squamous cell lung cancer secretes PTH-related peptide causing hypercalcaemia.

questions.pearl: Small cell lung cancer: ACTH and ADH (SIADH); squamous cell: PTHrP and hypercalcaemia.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.text: Obstructed labour is a common cause
options.explanation: In Bangladesh, pressure necrosis in prolonged obstructed labour is the commonest cause.

options.label: B
options.text: Three swab (cotton ball) test is a diagnostic procedure
options.explanation: Methylene blue in the bladder staining the swabs confirms and localises the fistula.

options.label: C
options.text: Common treatment is laparotomy and repair
options.explanation: Most VVFs are repaired by the vaginal route; abdominal repair is reserved for high fistulae.

options.label: D
options.text: Presence of an IUCD for a long time
options.explanation: IUCD does not cause VVF; prolonged pessary use may.

questions.pearl: Repair an obstetric VVF after about 3 months, once slough has separated and tissues are healthy.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Therapeutic index is a measure of:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Potency is the dose required for a given effect (EC50).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Efficacy is the maximal effect a drug can produce (Emax).

options.label: C
options.explanation: TI = TD50/ED50 (or LD50/ED50); a high TI means a wide safety margin.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Bioavailability is the fraction of drug reaching systemic circulation.

questions.pearl: Narrow therapeutic index drugs need monitoring: digoxin, lithium, warfarin, phenytoin, theophylline, aminoglycosides.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Magnesium sulphate relaxes the uterus (tocolytic) and is used for eclampsia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Oxytocin is the first-line uterotonic for preventing and treating PPH.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Misoprostol and carboprost cause strong uterine contraction.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Ergometrine causes sustained tetanic contraction; avoid in hypertension.

questions.pearl: Tocolytics (uterine relaxants): nifedipine, indomethacin, MgSO4, atosiban (oxytocin antagonist), beta-agonists.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.text: IgE takes part in parasitic infection and type 1 hypersensitivity
options.explanation: Key corrected: IgE binds mast cells and eosinophils, mediating type 1 hypersensitivity and defence against helminths.

options.label: B
options.explanation: IgM can neutralise toxins and viruses, though IgG is the main antitoxin antibody.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Secretory IgA (dimer with secretory piece) protects mucosal surfaces and is in breast milk.

options.label: D
options.explanation: IgG activates complement by the classical pathway (IgG3 most strongly).

questions.pearl: IgG is the only immunoglobulin to cross the placenta; IgM is the largest and first to appear.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Reduced LDL receptor expression raises LDL cholesterol.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Cholestasis raises cholesterol and lipoprotein X.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hypercholesterolaemia is a feature of nephrotic syndrome, not nephritic AGN.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Type 2 DM chiefly causes hypertriglyceridaemia with low HDL.

questions.pearl: Secondary hypercholesterolaemia: hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, cholestasis, anorexia nervosa, drugs (thiazides, ciclosporin).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Key corrected: sodium and water retention causes hypervolaemia, oedema, hypertension and circulatory overload.

options.label: B
options.explanation: AGN does not affect glucose metabolism.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Reduced GFR and oliguria impair potassium excretion.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Water retention exceeding sodium retention causes dilutional hyponatraemia.

questions.pearl: Post-streptococcal GN: low C3, raised ASO, cola-coloured urine 1-3 weeks after sore throat.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Abrupt high fever with myalgia (especially calves) is typical.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Weil's disease causes jaundice with renal failure and haemorrhage.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Leptospirosis is treated with antibiotics: penicillin or doxycycline.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Aseptic meningitis occurs in the immune phase.

questions.pearl: Leptospirosis is spread by rat urine; conjunctival suffusion is a characteristic sign.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Key corrected: mumps incubation is 16-18 days (range 2-4 weeks), as per Nelson and Park.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Rabies incubation is usually 1-3 months, shorter with head and neck bites.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Primary TB lesion or tuberculin conversion develops in about 3-12 weeks.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Measles incubation is about 10 days to fever and 14 days to rash.

questions.pearl: Shortest incubation: staphylococcal food poisoning (1-6 hours); longest variable: rabies and leprosy.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Initiates abduction; the most commonly torn cuff muscle.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Lateral rotator of the shoulder.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Teres major is not part of the cuff; it inserts on the medial lip of the bicipital groove.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Lateral rotator supplied by the axillary nerve.

questions.pearl: Rotator cuff (SITS): Supraspinatus, Infraspinatus, Teres minor, Subscapularis.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Fat provides 9 kcal/g and is the main energy store.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Carbohydrate gives 4 kcal/g and is the main fuel for the brain and RBCs.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Protein gives 4 kcal/g and is used in starvation via gluconeogenesis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Enzymes are catalysts, not fuels.

questions.pearl: In prolonged starvation the brain switches to ketone bodies, sparing muscle protein.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Retropharyngeal lymph nodes regress after about 5 years, so it is a disease of young children.

options.label: B
options.explanation: TB of the cervical spine causes chronic retropharyngeal abscess.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Acute abscess arises from suppurative nodes; vertebrae are spared.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Acute abscess causes high fever; low-grade fever suggests chronic tubercular abscess.

questions.pearl: Chronic retropharyngeal abscess lies in the midline (behind prevertebral fascia); acute lies to one side.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Sympathetic paralysis causes miosis, ptosis and anhidrosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Bilateral pinpoint pupils occur due to sympathetic tract interruption.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Oxytocin has no pupillary effect.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cocaine blocks noradrenaline reuptake and causes mydriasis.

questions.pearl: Pinpoint pupils: opioids, organophosphates, pontine haemorrhage.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Bacitracin inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis; used topically.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Aztreonam is a monobactam active against Gram-negative bacteria.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pyrimethamine is an antiprotozoal DHFR inhibitor used in toxoplasmosis and malaria.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Etoricoxib is a COX-2 selective NSAID.

questions.pearl: Aztreonam has no cross-allergy with penicillins, so can be used in penicillin-allergic patients.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Glucocorticoids alter metabolism but are not used or classed as metabolic rate stimulants.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Caffeine increases thermogenesis via sympathetic activation and PDE inhibition.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Cimetidine is an H2 blocker and enzyme inhibitor with no BMR effect.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Nicotine raises metabolic rate via catecholamine release.

questions.pearl: Thyroxine is the main hormone raising basal metabolic rate; BMR falls in hypothyroidism.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Posterior hypothalamic lesions impair heat conservation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Anterior hypothalamic lesions impair heat loss.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hypothalamic-limbic disruption causes emotional disturbance.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Rage, emotional lability and behavioural change are recognised.

questions.pearl: Hypothalamic lesions also cause diabetes insipidus, obesity (ventromedial) and disordered sleep.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.text: Thickening of the inner layer of skin
options.explanation: Hyperkeratosis affects the stratum corneum, the outermost layer, not the dermis.

options.label: B
options.text: Thickening of the outer layer of skin
options.explanation: It is thickening of the stratum corneum.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Calluses and corns at pressure points may be painful.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Chronic friction, irritants (e.g. arsenic) and inflammation induce hyperkeratosis.

questions.pearl: Arsenicosis in Bangladesh: palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and raindrop pigmentation.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Broad-based ataxic gait, falling to the side of the lesion.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Cerebellar dysarthria is slurred and scanning.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Extensor plantar is an upper motor neurone sign.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Clasp-knife spasticity is pyramidal; cerebellar lesions cause hypotonia.

questions.pearl: Cerebellar signs (DANISH): Dysdiadochokinesia, Ataxia, Nystagmus, Intention tremor, Speech, Hypotonia.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Bony malleoli are pressure points in the lateral position.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The greater trochanter, not the deep lesser trochanter, is a pressure site.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Ischial tuberosities are pressure points when sitting.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The sacrum is the commonest site in supine patients.

questions.pearl: Prevent pressure sores by turning every 2 hours; grade using the NPUAP/EPUAP staging (1-4).

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Profuse watery rhinorrhoea with sneezing is typical.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Turbinates are oedematous and pale/bluish; hypertrophy (mainly inferior) occurs only in chronic cases.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Epistaxis is not a typical feature.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Mucosal oedema and polyps can cause hyposmia or anosmia.

questions.pearl: Allergic rhinitis signs: allergic salute, allergic shiners, Dennie-Morgan lines, pale boggy turbinates.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Urine output is a monitoring parameter, not a preoperative investigation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Complete blood count detects anaemia and infection before surgery.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Ultrasonography is part of preoperative workup for many abdominal procedures.

options.label: D
options.explanation: CXR is indicated in elderly, smokers and patients with cardiorespiratory disease.

questions.pearl: Preoperative assessment: ASA grading; routine tests are guided by age, comorbidity and surgical grade.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: A dense ring around an osteopenic epiphysis is characteristic.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Metaphyseal fraying and cupping are features of rickets.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Widened physis gap is a rickets feature; scurvy shows a lucent Trummerfeld zone.

options.label: D
options.text: Lateral spurring at the white line (Pelkan spur)
options.explanation: Spurs extend from the dense white line of Frankel.

questions.pearl: Scurvy X-ray: ground-glass bone, pencil-thin cortex, Wimberger ring, Frankel line, corner sign, Pelkan spur.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Volume overload causes eccentric left ventricular hypertrophy and dilatation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Raised left atrial pressure causes exertional dyspnoea.

options.label: C
options.explanation: MR produces a systolic thrill; a diastolic apical thrill suggests mitral stenosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Apical pansystolic murmur radiating to the axilla is classic.

questions.pearl: Severe MR: soft S1, S3 and laterally displaced apex beat.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Bisoprolol is highly beta-1 selective and used in heart failure.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Carvedilol is a non-selective beta blocker with alpha-1 blocking activity.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Atenolol is beta-1 selective and renally excreted.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Propranolol is non-selective; avoid in asthma.

questions.pearl: Cardioselective beta blockers (BEAM): Bisoprolol, Esmolol, Atenolol, Metoprolol (also nebivolol).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: VC is the maximum volume exhaled after a maximal inspiration.

options.label: B
options.text: Equals the sum of inspiratory reserve, tidal and expiratory reserve volumes
options.explanation: VC = IRV + TV + ERV.

options.label: C
options.explanation: About 4.6 L in a normal young male; less in women.

options.label: D
options.explanation: VC is measured by spirometry; residual volume is not.

questions.pearl: Residual volume, FRC and TLC cannot be measured by simple spirometry; use helium dilution or body plethysmography.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Seizures over 5 minutes or recurring without recovery need immediate treatment.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Transverse myelitis is managed urgently but is usually inflammatory and less time-critical than compression.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Needs urgent MRI and decompression to preserve function.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Guillain-Barre syndrome can cause respiratory failure; monitor FVC.

questions.pearl: In GBS, intubate if FVC falls below 20 ml/kg; treat with IVIG or plasma exchange.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Components of the Glasgow Coma Scale:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pupils are assessed separately; they are not part of GCS.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Scored 1-6.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Scored 1-5.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Scored 1-4.

questions.pearl: GCS ranges 3-15; a score of 8 or less indicates the need for airway protection.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Adequate calcium protects bone; low intake predisposes to osteoporosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Inflammatory cytokines and immobility cause periarticular and generalised osteoporosis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Enzyme-inducing anticonvulsants increase vitamin D catabolism.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Glucocorticoids are the commonest cause of secondary osteoporosis.

questions.pearl: Osteoporosis is a DXA T-score of -2.5 or less; bisphosphonates are first-line treatment.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Butterfly rash sparing the nasolabial folds is classic.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Immune complex vasculitis is part of SLE.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Discoid erythematous lesions are a classification criterion.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pleuritis and pericarditis are common.

questions.pearl: Anti-dsDNA and anti-Smith are specific for SLE; anti-histone suggests drug-induced lupus.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Purpura over the buttocks and extensor lower limbs with normal platelets.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Colicky pain from bowel vasculitis; intussusception may occur.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Large joints, especially knees and ankles, are involved.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Key corrected: GI vasculitis causes pain, vomiting and bleeding, not constipation.

questions.pearl: HSP is IgA vasculitis; long-term prognosis depends on renal involvement.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: PTH increases calcium reabsorption in the distal tubule.

options.label: B
options.text: Increases calcium mobilisation from bone to ECF
options.explanation: PTH stimulates osteoclastic bone resorption via RANKL.

options.label: C
options.explanation: PTH inhibits proximal tubular phosphate reabsorption.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Phosphaturia is a classic PTH effect.

questions.pearl: PTH also stimulates 1-alpha-hydroxylase in the kidney, raising calcitriol.
